_comment: The Reading (Expansion 6 F.4, docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.7; game/story/reading.py): the Wayfarer's Deck (the game's own: twenty great cards and four suits), its seers, the five places of a reading and the words a riddle is written with. The truth comes first: the game knows the answer, picks the card whose tags fit it best and writes the riddle from the real place's or person's own past. {where} and {look} are phrases that follow 'lies' ('where, in 913, ...', 'under old trees'); {who} follows a verb's subject ('one who fells trees').

door.name: The Door
door.asks: where the last stand will be

lantern.name: the Lantern
lantern.meaning: a light carried into the dark; what is hidden, found
signs: A lamp burns in a window in broad day, as if someone inside had forgotten to put it out
Someone has hung a lantern on a nail here, long cold, its horn panes gone yellow
A little shrine-lamp sits in a niche in the stone, still smoking
marks: a little horn lantern hangs from {their} belt, unlit
{they} carr{ies} a lamp even by day, out of habit
{their} fingers smell of lamp oil, and a flint hangs at {their} belt

hound.name: the Hound
hound.meaning: loyalty that follows to the end
signs: A grey hound lies across the way, watches you pass, and does not bark
Paw prints in the mud here, a big dog's, going the way you are going
A dog's collar hangs from a post, its brass worn bright by a hand
marks: a lean hound follows at {their} heel and never takes its eyes off {them}
there are dog hairs all over {their} coat, and a whistle on a cord at {their} neck
{their} hand drops, now and then, to the height of a dog's head, though no dog is there

widow.name: the Widow
widow.meaning: one who has lost, and goes on
signs: A woman in black stands at a door here, and goes in when she sees you
Black ribbons are tied to a post, faded grey by the weather
A wreath of dried flowers hangs by the way, the kind left for the dead
marks: {they} wear{s} a black band on {their} arm, frayed with long wearing
{they} turn{s} a ring on {their} finger that is too big for it, and was never {theirs}
{their} sleeves are black, and mended in black thread, and have been so a long while

ford.name: the Ford
ford.meaning: a crossing; where the water is shallow enough to fight
signs: Water talks over stones somewhere close, and the path goes down to meet it
Flat stepping-stones lie across a stream here, one of them broken
The ground is churned at the water's edge, where many feet have crossed
marks: {their} boots are wet to the knee, as if {they} had just come across a river
{they} {have} the look of someone who has waded a great many cold rivers
{their} cloak is stiff with old river mud to the hem

crown.name: the Crown
crown.meaning: power, and what it costs to keep it
signs: A lord's arms are carved over the way in, half chiselled off by someone later
A gilt circlet is painted on a sign here, flaking
Somebody has scratched a little crown into the stone, the kind children draw
marks: {their} cloak is pinned with a brooch too fine for the rest of {them}
{they} sit{s} as if in a high seat, even on a bench
{they} wait{s} to be answered, a moment too long, as one used to it

bell.name: the Bell
bell.meaning: a warning rung too late, or just in time
signs: A bell rings somewhere as you come, once, and stops
An old bronze bell hangs from a frame here, green, with no rope
The cracked half of a bell lies in the grass, too heavy for anyone to have carried off
marks: a little bell is sewn to {their} sleeve, and it rings when {they} move{s}
{they} start{s} at every bell, and then pretend{s} {they} did not
{their} voice drops whenever a bell sounds, and {they} count{s} the strokes under {their} breath

mask.name: the Mask
mask.meaning: a face that is not the face beneath
signs: A painted mask is nailed up here, the kind worn at a midwinter play, grinning
A face is carved into a post, and turned to the wall
Someone has left a mummer's mask in the mud, face down
marks: {they} smile{s} a moment before {they} mean{s} it
{their} face gives nothing away at all, which is a thing in itself
{they} change{s} {their} manner with each person {they} speak{s} to, and no two are alike

key.name: the Key
key.meaning: what was locked, and the way in
signs: An iron key hangs from a nail beside the way in, too big for any lock you can see
A lock lies broken on the ground here, the hasp still bright where it was forced
Keyholes are carved into the stone here, three of them, leading nowhere
marks: a ring of keys hangs at {their} belt, more than anyone could need
{they} keep{s} one hand on something in {their} pocket, small and hard
{their} fingers go to a key at {their} throat on a cord, and away again

ash_tree.name: the Ash Tree
signs: An old ash stands over the way, split by lightning long ago and growing still
Roots break the stones here, older than the stones
A tree has been planted by the way, by someone who meant it to outlive them
marks: {their} hands are as hard and knotted as roots
there is sawdust in {their} hair, and the smell of new-cut ash
{they} smell{s} of green wood and sap, and {their} boots are caked with forest loam

bride.name: the Bride
bride.meaning: a promise made, and the price of keeping it
signs: A wedding garland hangs over a door here, the flowers dry as paper
Two names are carved together in the wood, and one of them scratched out
Somebody has tied a white ribbon to a branch here, the way they do for a vow
marks: {they} wear{s} a plaited ring of grass, the kind given in a promise
{they} speak{s} of a promise {they} made, and change{s} the subject
{their} left hand bears a pale band where a ring was, and {they} cover{s} it

smith.name: the Smith
smith.meaning: what is made strong by fire and by blows
signs: A smith's sign hangs over a door here, a hammer and tongs cut from tin
A horseshoe is nailed over the way in, rusted the colour of old blood
The ground here is black with old cinders, as if a forge once stood
marks: {their} forearms are spotted with little white burn scars
{they} smell{s} of iron and of the forge
{their} apron is scorched, and {their} palms are hard as horn

pilgrim.name: the Pilgrim
pilgrim.meaning: the long road, walked for a reason
signs: A stone by the way is worn smooth on top, where pilgrims have touched it for luck
A walking staff leans against the wall here, left by someone who did not need it any more
Scallop shells are pressed into the mortar here, a pilgrim's mark
marks: {their} boots have been mended many more times than they were made
{they} {have} the long stride of someone who walks a great deal
a scallop shell hangs from {their} pack, worn smooth by many roads

sleeper.name: the Sleeper
sleeper.meaning: what lies down and does not stay down
signs: A stone figure lies on its back here, hands folded, its face worn away
The grass grows in the shape of a long mound, as over something buried
It is very quiet here, the quiet of a room where someone is asleep
marks: {they} look{s} as if {they} {have} not slept in a long while
{their} eyes close, now and then, as if {they} heard something far off
{their} voice is slow, as if {they} spoke out of a dream

broken_shield.name: the Broken Shield
signs: Half a shield is nailed up here, split down the middle, its paint long gone
Rusted iron lies in the grass here, the bits of something that broke
A cairn of stones stands by the way, the kind raised after a battle
marks: {they} carr{ies} an old scar across the knuckles, the kind a shield-rim gives
{they} stand{s} like a soldier, and do{es} not like to be reminded of it
{they} {have} a dent in {their} helm, and no wish to tell how it came there

crow.name: the Crow
crow.meaning: the one who comes after; an omen of the dead
signs: A crow sits on a post here and watches you, and does not fly
Black feathers lie scattered on the ground, a great many
Crows rise from somewhere close as you come, and settle again behind you
marks: a black feather is stuck in {their} hat
{they} watch{es} the crows as other people watch the weather
{their} coat is black and ragged at the hem, like a bird's wing

mother.name: the Mother
signs: A child's toy lies by the way, a wooden horse with one leg gone
Herbs are drying over a door here, the kind hung against sickness
A woman calls children in from somewhere close, and they come
marks: {they} {have} a child's drawing folded small in {their} coat
{they} fuss{es} over everyone, as if they were {their} own
{their} pockets hold bread-ends and ribbon and a child's mitten

grave.name: the Grave
grave.meaning: the end that waits for all; a resting place disturbed
signs: A grave lies open by the way, and the earth beside it is fresh
Old headstones lean here, the names gone from them
The ground is sunken here in a long shape, as over a coffin that has given way
marks: there is graveyard clay dried on {their} boots
{they} speak{s} of the dead as if they were in the next room
{their} hands are grey with earth under the nails, however often they are washed

wheel.name: the Wheel
wheel.meaning: time turning; the scheme moves on
signs: A broken cartwheel leans against the wall here, its spokes like a clock's hands
A millwheel turns somewhere close, slow and patient
Ruts run deep here, worn by years of wheels
marks: {they} keep{s} counting the days on {their} fingers
{they} turn{s} a little wooden wheel in {their} fingers when {they} think{s}
{they} look{s} at the sun more than at the road, as if reckoning how much of the day is gone

candle.name: the Candle
candle.meaning: a small light against the night; hope, and little time
signs: A stub of candle stands in a niche here, burned almost to nothing
Wax drippings cover a stone here, where people have lit candles for years
One candle burns in a window, though nobody is in the room
marks: {their} fingers are spotted with old candle-wax
{they} carr{ies} a candle-end in {their} pocket, against the dark
{they} shield{s} a small flame with a cupped hand, even indoors, where there is no wind

wolf.name: the Wolf
wolf.meaning: hunger that will not be reasoned with
signs: Wolf tracks cross the way here, a big animal's, going north
Bones lie gnawed by the way, an old kill
A wolf's skull is nailed over the way in, by someone who wanted it seen
marks: {they} wear{s} a wolf's tooth on a thong
{they} eat{s} like someone who has been hungry, and remembers it
{their} eyes follow every scrap of food on the table

cups.name: Cups
cups.meaning: the heart: love, grief and faith

key: The thing you will need is kept {where}.
Go looking {where}, {look}, and you will find what you need.
door: The last of it will be {where}, {look}.
You will face it {where}. The cards are sure of that.
There is a door {where}, {look}, and beyond it the end.
hand: {who} will stand with you, when it counts.
Trust {who}. There will be a day you need to.
The cards give you {who}. Do not turn them away.
{who}: that one is true, whatever else is not.
shadow: Even it is afraid of something: {fear}.
Look for {fear}. It cannot abide it.
turn_traitor: One of yours is not yours: {tell}.
There is a mask at your table: {tell}.

a village

a hold under the mountain

beast: {seer}'s lips draw back from the teeth, and something looks out through the eyes that is not a person at all. It has your scent now. It turns, slowly, toward the card of the Hand, and the fire gutters.
{seer} growls, low, a sound no throat like that should make, and sets one finger on the card of the Hand as if marking prey. Then the fire flares, and {seer} is only frightened and old.
risen: "You read the bones of my kingdom," says a voice that is not {seer}'s, dry as a shut tomb. "Read them, then. I will come for the one your cards favour."

{seer}'s breath smokes in the warm air. "Cards," says something with that mouth, very old and very patient. "I had a seer once. I had them all, at the end. Tell the one the Hand names that I am coming."
outlaw: "Cards," says {seer}, in a man's voice, laughing. "I'll tell your fortune for you, friend, with a knife. And your friend's, the one on the card there."

"Pretty," says a voice from {seer}'s mouth that belongs in a tavern brawl. "Now I know who to visit first." {seer}'s hand slaps down on the card of the Hand, and then {seer} is blinking, not knowing why.
default: {seer} goes rigid. "{villain} sees you," says a voice that is not {seer}'s, "and the one the cards favour."

silent_words: The card will not speak. "Not yet," says {seer}. "Come back when the road has turned."
{seer} turns the card, and frowns at it. "Blank to me. Ask again when the tale has moved on."
Smoke from the fire hangs over this one, and will not lift. "Later," {seer} says. "It is not ready to be read."
pointed: {sign}. You think of {seer}'s fire, and {card} turning over.
met: You notice that {mark}, and think of {card} in {seer}'s hands.
shadow_seen: You remember {card} in {seer}'s fire: {fear}. The cards were right.

ask: Will you read the cards for me?
They say you can see what is coming. Read for me.
none: "The cards have nothing to say to you yet," says {seer}. "Come back when the road has chosen you."
{seer} looks at you a long time, and shakes {their} head. "No tale has its hooks in you yet. Nothing to read."
done: "I have read for you once in this," says {seer}. "The cards do not like to be asked twice. When the road turns, come back."
"Not again so soon," {seer} says. "Come back when the tale has moved on, and the silent cards may speak."
yes: {seer} is already shuffling. "Sit down by the fire."
"Sit," says {seer}, and moves a pot off the coals to make room for the cards.

seer: {seer} keeps a fire at the edge of {place}, under a patched awning, where the roads meet. The cards are old and soft as cloth, and smell of woodsmoke.
{seer}'s fire is the last one before the open road. {seer} spreads a square of faded red cloth beside it and does not look up at you, only at the cards.
There is a smell of herbs and smoke, a three-legged pot on the coals, and {seer}, who has been waiting for you, or says so.
hermit: {seer} lives at {place} in a shelter of stones and turf, and has for longer than anyone remembers. The fire is small and the cards are smaller, worn almost round.
{seer} comes out of the rocks at {place} as if expecting you, and sits by a little fire, and takes out a deck of cards wrapped in a hide.

asks: "A coin," says {seer}, "or a favour. The cards do not care which. I do."
"Cross my palm," says {seer}, "or carry water for my fire. Either is payment."
"The cards want something of you first," says {seer}. "Silver, or an hour of your work."
hermits: the old one who lives at {wonder}
